proposed_widenings.name: stored_spell_energy_as_slot_substitution
proposed_widenings.justification: The rod's primary spend-side mechanic is not named-spell access. It lets a spellcaster spend stored levels from the item instead of expending their own spell slots when casting any spell they already have prepared or know, subject to slot-level caps. The current surface can grant named spells from item charges, but it cannot express arbitrary spell-slot substitution against the wielder's existing spell list.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "If you are a spellcaster holding the rod, you can convert energy stored in it into spell slots to cast spells you have prepared or know. You can create spell slots only of a level equal to or lower than your own spell slots, up to a maximum of level 5. You use the stored levels in place of your slots but otherwise cast the spell as normal."

proposed_widenings.name: composite_magic_item_part_triggered_reaction
proposed_widenings.justification: The absorption half is a reaction-shaped item ability that spends from the same stored-energy pool the rod later uses for slot substitution. The current top-level magic-item union supports triggered reactions, but the authored composite family only works if every part can be represented honestly; this rod needs the reaction part combined with the missing slot-substitution part.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "While holding this rod, you can take a Reaction to absorb a spell that is targeting only you and doesn't create an area of effect."

proposed_widenings.name: item_becomes_nonmagical_when_lifetime_absorption_cap_reached_and_pool_empty
proposed_widenings.justification: The current surface can model a lifetime absorption cap on a charge pool, but not the follow-on state change that occurs only when both conditions are true: the rod has already absorbed 50 total levels over its existence and it has no stored energy remaining. That is a specific lifecycle gate, not simple destruction on empty.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "The rod can absorb and store up to 50 levels of energy over the course of its existence. Once the rod absorbs 50 levels of energy, it can't absorb more." and "A rod that can no longer absorb spell energy and has no energy remaining becomes nonmagical."

notes: I did not author a placeholder content file. The reaction-side absorption can be expressed with existing reaction trigger filters plus negate/cancel behavior and a charge pool with lifetimeAbsorptionCap, but the item's core spend-side mechanic is arbitrary spell-slot substitution for the wielder's own prepared/known spells, which the current surface cannot encode honestly.
